file-catalog-with-saved-data-01.graded_text: Saved data is reached through the same read, write, exact-edit, and delete-file tools used for source files and assets, as file paths such as JSON files. The catalog has no separate tools for records, entries, collections, or the database.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:31 lists a separate entry tool: "| `add_saved_entries` | Add new entries to a saved-data collection |", and line 274 makes it mandatory: "Writing to an entry path that doesn't exist is refused with `entry_not_found`, which points to `add_saved_entries`." Reads, replaces, edits and deletes do go through the file tools under `@saved/` (line 7), but the catalog still has a separate tool for creating entries in collections.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-02.graded_text: No tool has a required idempotency key, revision or version token, or confirmation argument. Protection against stale writes is enforced by the server, for example by rejecting a write that would overwrite changes made since the agent's read and asking for a fresh read.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:358 "Lost updates are guarded on the server, not with a token the agent must carry ... that item is refused with `stale_read`, which asks for a fresh `read_file`." Line 35: "No tool takes a confirmation flag". Line 408: "No idempotency keys on `create_site` or `add_saved_entries`." I checked every schema (lines 138-344). No revision, version, idempotency or confirm argument appears. The nearest is the optional `replace_all?: boolean` on edit_file (line 304), which only controls how many matches are replaced and confirms nothing.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-03.graded_text: The design explains how a visitor's write made after the agent read a saved-data file survives the agent's later write of that file: it is merged safely or the agent's write fails with a conflict. A plain last-writer-wins replacement does not pass.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:358 "Say `write_files` would replace an existing file or entry, and its current revision isn't one this connection saw (for example, a visitor updated the RSVP after the agent read it). Then that item is refused with `stale_read`". Line 310 covers edits: "If a visitor changed a different field of the same entry in the meantime, the edit still applies and keeps the visitor's change." Whole replacement fails with a conflict, and an exact edit merges, so neither is last-writer-wins.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-04.graded_text: Deleting files takes an explicit nonempty list of exact paths, deleting a whole site is its own tool, and no omitted argument widens a deletion or makes an update create a new site.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:323 `paths: string[];   // 1..100 exact file or entry paths`. Line 327: "Directory paths, collection paths, and wildcards are refused with `not_a_file`." delete_site is its own tool taking a required `{ site_id: string }` (line 195). write_files/edit_file require `site_id` (lines 268, 299), and only create_site creates a site. The only optional destructive argument is `replace_all?` (line 304), which defaults to false, so omitting it narrows the edit.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-05.graded_text: Writing a saved-data file as a whole is checked entry by entry against the site's declared write rules and validation, with the agent holding only the rights of the person it acts for, so replacing the whole file cannot make a change that person could not make one entry at a time.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:7 "A file operation on `@saved/` runs the same per-entry product mutation the visitor runtime SDK uses, with the same validation, quota, and live push to open pages. Replacing a whole entry file changes only that entry." Line 357: "No file-view operation touches more than one entry, except batches, where each item is its own mutation." Line 399: "An agent acts as the person who connected it". Line 84: "Owners can always write every entry. The rules decide what visitors can do." That matches the brief's "or by the site owner". Since each entry is its own file, a whole-file write can't touch more than one entry.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-06.graded_text: There is no separate tool or argument for setting a site's title, description, or favicon. They come from index.html.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:183 "There are no title, description, or favicon arguments. Fernpage reads them from `index.html`." The Site type (lines 97-99) marks each field as "from index.html". I checked every tool schema (lines 138-344) and none sets them.
